settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Mesh DNS, Gateway filtering, maintenance, and WARP split tunnels.

meshDns.title: Automatic Mesh DNS
meshDns.description: Configure the base domain suffix used for auto-registering mesh hostnames across your devices and connectors.
meshDns.syncNotice: Changing this suffix automatically triggers a full DNS resynchronization.
meshDns.warpFallbackWarning: Warning: .{{suffix}} is in Cloudflare WARP's Local Domain Fallback list and will bypass Gateway DNS resolution.

cleanup.title: Offline Device Cleanup
cleanup.description: Automatically purge enrolled devices and ephemeral nodes that have been offline longer than the retention threshold.

splitTunnels.title: WARP Split Tunnels
splitTunnels.description: Control whether internal traffic is excluded from or routed through Cloudflare Zero Trust WARP client.
splitTunnels.loadFailed: Could not load split tunnel rules.
splitTunnels.modeExcludeHint: All traffic goes through WARP except the listed destinations.
splitTunnels.modeIncludeHint: Only listed destinations go through WARP.
splitTunnels.switchWarning: Switching to {{mode}} mode clears the current list, because Cloudflare keeps only one list per mode. This cannot be undone.
splitTunnels.auditWarning: Warning: Mesh network subnet (100.64.0.0/10) is currently excluded, which prevents mesh routing.
splitTunnels.meshRoutingFixed: Split tunnels updated to route Mesh IPs through WARP.
splitTunnels.movedHint: Split tunnels and routes moved to the Routing page.

dnsFilter.title: DNS Filtering
dnsFilter.description: Block malware, phishing, and ad trackers at the Cloudflare Gateway DNS layer.

gateway.description: Dedicated DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) and IPv4 Anycast endpoints provisioned for your Zero Trust location.
gateway.noLocation: No default Gateway DNS location found.

maintenance.description: Audit synchronicity between meshflare state and Cloudflare Gateway policies.
maintenance.healthyNotice: All Cloudflare Zero Trust configurations are fully synchronized and healthy.
maintenance.degradedNotice: Desynchronization detected between database state and Cloudflare Gateway.

routing.title: Routing
routing.bulkCount: Entries: {{count}}. Separate with new lines, spaces or commas.
routing.switchWarning: Switching {{profile}} to {{mode}} mode replaces its current list, because Cloudflare keeps one list per mode. Devices in this profile pick up the change within a minute.

check.label: Check a destination
check.idle: Type a hostname, URL or IP to see where this profile sends it.
check.notIncluded: not in this profile's Include list
check.blocked: Routed to {{exit}}, but never gets there
check.blockedDetail: This profile does not send 172.64.128.0/20 through WARP, and hostname routes need that range.

split.hintExclude: These go straight out the local network. Everything else goes through WARP.
split.hintInclude: Only these go through WARP. Everything else goes straight out the local network.
split.addDesc: Adds to the {{profile}} profile. Use *.example.com for subdomains; example.com alone matches only itself.

routes.title: Routes
routes.hint: Send a hostname or network out through a specific tunnel or Mesh node. Applies to every device, whatever its profile.
routes.empty: No routes. Traffic not bypassed goes out through Cloudflare.
routes.addDesc: Hostnames are routed by name (Gateway DNS must be in use). IPs and CIDRs are routed as networks.
routes.valuesHint: example.com also covers every subdomain (www.example.com, cdn.example.com).
routes.nodeHostnameTitle: Hostnames routed to a Mesh node
routes.nodeHostnameBody: {{hosts}} exit through a Mesh node. The node looks these names up through Gateway, which refuses names routed to it, so they stop resolving on every device unless the node has them in its hosts file. Send internet sites to a tunnel instead.
routes.nodeHostnameWarn: A Mesh node can only exit hostnames it can look up without Gateway (for example, from its hosts file). Otherwise these names stop resolving for every device. Use a tunnel for internet sites.

mesh_not_routed.title: Mesh IPs are not routed
mesh_not_routed.body: This profile is in Include mode without 100.96.0.0/12, so .mesh hostnames are unreachable.

mesh_bypassed.title: Mesh IPs bypass WARP
mesh_bypassed.body: {{subject}} is excluded, which covers the Mesh range 100.96.0.0/12.

resolved_ip_bypassed.title: Hostname routes are bypassed
resolved_ip_bypassed.body: {{subject}} is excluded and covers 172.64.128.0/20, the range Gateway uses for routed hostnames.

resolved_ip_not_included.title: Hostname routes do not apply here
resolved_ip_not_included.body: Include mode without 172.64.128.0/20, so routed hostnames never reach their exit on these devices.

route_bypassed.title: Route overridden by bypass
route_bypassed.body: {{subject}} has a route, but this profile bypasses it, so it goes direct.

tunnel.routesHint: Hostnames and networks listed here leave through this tunnel for every device. Manage all routes on the Routing page.

profiles.emailsHint: Separate addresses with spaces, commas or new lines.
